steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat a 9x13-inch baking pan with cooking spray.

Whisk flour, sugar, salt, cinnamon, and baking soda together in a large bowl. Whisk oil, eggs, and vanilla extract together in a separate bowl; stir into flour mixture until combined. Fold in chopped apples until just combined.
Pour batter into the prepared baking pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into center comes out clean, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Adam's Apple Cake
raw_recipe.description: Adam's apple cake recipe is simple to make yet incredibly flavorful, and it only requires apples, basic pantry ingredients, and a 9x13-inch baking pan.

video.description: Meet 10 year-old baker, Adam, and see how to make his favorite recipe.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely delicious, addictive, and easy to make! Batter is thick but bakes up light with great texture. My fiancee actually found this recipe and started it- i hesitated because of the lack of reviews. I am SO glad he convinced me to make this. We have made it 3 times in 3 days adding brown sugar, raisins, and walnuts. You will not be disappointed!

Just baked this cake late yesterday. Followed the recipe except, while I was peeling and coring the apples, I poured some pasteurized orange juice (not from concentrate if that matters) over the cut apples (2 large Gala and 3 small Rome) to keep them from browning (about 3/4 to a cup) while I finished preparing the rest of the apples. Once finished with the apples, started mixing the dry and wet ingredients. The batter came out very crumbly, so I poured some of the juice from the prepared apples into the batter to make it come together (MUCH better). Folded in the rest of the juicy apples and poured into glass baking dish (9x13) sprayed with baker's joy. Used a silicon spatula to push any protruding apples down into the batter and put in the oven for one hour. I AM NOT a baker normally, but this cake is AWESOME!!! The hardest part is preparing the apples but it's DEFINITELY worth the effort. I'll be making this again and again! Thanks to the poster and all the previous reviewers. This cake tastes like the Jewish apple cake my late mother used to make...thanks for the fond memories!

I baked this cake late yesterday. This morning it went well with my morning coffee. I did make some changes. First I greased and floured my cake pan instead of using cooking spray. It called for 4 apples. I pared and chopped 4 small apples but only used half of them. I added some whole milk to make the batter more like a cake batter than cookie dough. I also added about 3/4 cup chopped walnuts. Since the recipe did not say how long to bake it I went by what other cake recipes recommend and baked it 50 minutes. I don't know if I will bake this recipe again or not but if I do I will probably add more oil to make it moister. It does make a pretty good coffee cake.

This is a great apple cake and easy to make. I've done with half brown sugar and half white, just because I like the flavor of brown sugar. Doesn't matter because I'd make it either way. :-) I've also cut the recipe in half and used in an 8x8 pan. Any negative reviews are a mystery to me, but to each his own. I've already saved this as a favorite and will certainly make it again. Thank you for the recipe!

Okay... in short this turned out delicious. I followed the recipe almost exactly, but I used butter instead of oil and consequently had to add about 1/2 a cup of milk - and nutmeg. I loooove nutmeg. My batter looked NOTHING like Adam's in the video. It was incredibly sticky and after cutting up only 3 avg sized apples, the bowl was more apple than batter... uh oh. Then I realize there is no 9X13 pan where I'm staying. 9X7?? Yikes. It's all I have; let's try it! 
After a good 70 minutes it was cooked through, 3 inches high, beautifully browned, and dense (more a bread than a cake, which I liked). I will make this again and again, and I truly don't think I'd make it any differently! I loved it! My husband loved it! (That said, I'm sitting here thinking I'd add some cranberries or raspberries for some 'bite'. Yum!) 

* At about the half hour mark I added a brown sugar and cinnamon topping and did cover the cake with foil for the last 20+ minutes of cooking.

I absolutely recommend this cake! Don't compare yours to the video! (Was it the oil substitution that did it? Not sure...).

Note: I am irked by ppl who rate things 5 stars yet have made several alterations to a recipe. I'm giving 5 because I "loved it", it's true, and I feel my modifications were because I had to work with what I had - a 9X7 pan - and I try never to use vegetable oil in anything.

I just pulled this cake out of the oven and he a tiny taste and it's great! I did make a few small changes to the recipe. I used a cup of oil and a cup of applesauce, instead of all oil. I also used half white sugar and half brown sugar. Added 4 Tblspoon of plain yogurt because we didn't have any sour cream. The batter was very moist, probably because of the applesauce. Baked the cake for one hour in a glass 9 x 13" pan @ 350 and it came out perfect. Thank you Adam and your family for a great recipe!

A suggestion that I tried that really made this moist was to whip the oil and eggs together first until they combined, then add the other liquid ingredients to that mixture. Mix all of the dry ingredients together before adding it to the wet. Add apples last and my family likes to add chopped walnuts. Great with coffee!

I followed the recipe and reviews. Batter was very thick even after increasing oil to 1 cup, and adding 1/4 cup buttermilk. I used 5 small gala apples. I made 2 at exactly the same time, baked at the same time, and one was done in 45 minutes, while the other one took the full hour to pass the toothpick test. The difference is that a metal pan cooks faster than a glass one! :) I also added a streusal topping of 2/3 cup flour, 2/3 cup sugar, 1/4 cup butter, 1/2 tsp cinnamon. I didn’t feel like icing it. LOL! Smells amazing here

I would say it's really 4.5 stars. I used half brown sugar and butter rather than oil. No electric mixer is necessary. I melted the butter, stirred in sugar, let it cool a minute then stirred in eggs and dry ingredients, followed by apples. It's a breeze to make with the pre-sliced apples from the produce section. An hour was way too long for mine to bake. Probably 40 min. at the max. Might benefit from a glaze or streusel.

This cake is delicious!! I have friends who have sensitive food allergies and I have made it with gluten free flour and/or white rice flower. I have also made it using apple sauce instead of the eggs. Making it gluten free, egg free and of course dairy free, for anyone who know someone with sensitive allergies or wants to try. If you do make it with the gluten free stuff after you are done mixing it all together spread it out in the baking dish and let it sit for about 5 minutes, the juices from the apples kind of help it settle. I always get a request for more!!

Such an amazing cake! If I didn't bake it myself I would of thought it was professionally made in a bakery somewhere. I had to make a little alteration to the recipe stated above. My "batter" was just all powder after I finished mixing it. I added 3/4 - 1 Cup of applesauce and about 1/4 cup of milk to make my batter a cake batter. The moisture and sweetness was just perfect!

My husband and I have been married 40 years. When we were dating. He brought me a piece of his mom's apple cake. This same recipe as you make it is a multi generational recipe for his family. It always reminds us of my husband's mother and grandmother. It fills us both we loving nostalgia. Easy to make and I will never change a thing. The way it is. Is what makes it so special to us both. Thank you.
I love this recipe exactly as written and if you hand mix everything - it is very simple. Family loves for breakfast/brunch or dessert with vanilla ice cream or fresh whipped cream. Thanks Adam!
Family favorite. Great with coffee for breakfast or with vanilla ice cream for dessert.

Were all the positive reviews left for this recipe submitted by family members? Absolutely horrible! Followed the recipe exactly. It doesn’t make batter, it makes dough. Totally crumbly and dry after baking. Nothing can salvage this mess! Something had to be left out of the recipe!!!!

First off - like other reviewers said, the batter was VERY thick. I tried using the hand mixer, Um, not so much. You may need to use the heavy duty mixer or have your husband mix it! I'm positive the cake would have been delicious without any changes, but I made a few, just because I know our taste buds. I added one TBS of cinnamon, an extra TSP of vanilla, used half brown and half white sugar and didn't bother peeling the apples. Delicious! (Oh, and I added golden raisins because we love those too!)
Simple and delicious! I will definitely make this again.

This is a very easy recipe to make. I'm glad a previous reviewer mentioned that the batter was thick. I ended up adding about 1/2 cup of milk to be able to moisten all that flour. It came out tender and moist! It did not last long enough to take a photo of it!

We really enjoyed this recipe. I will use a spice cake next time though with it. It was a nice looking bundt cake. It was frosted with a brown sugar glaze-add apple pie or pumpkin pie spice if you want a bit more flavor.
Easy to make and my wife really liked it !
